doc.title: Ametria Dock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 4, 2019

chapter: Church upbringing and singing on the spot
title: Singing 'Summertime' with the students: filling the space and letting it breathe
summary: Rowe notes she filled the gaps in 'Summertime' the previous night; Dock explains she sometimes sings over chord movement and sometimes lets it breathe.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I noticed last night when we did, we played “Summertime” and during those six, seven, eight beats after each line I was typically an accompanist goes okay I’m going to fill in there. But you filled in there, right?
I said, ah, okay, she’s got this.
I just, I love, and sometimes it just depends on when I’m singing and I’m kind of in the zone, when I hear different chords and different movements sometimes I like to sing over
them and sometimes I like to just let it breathe. But it felt really good last night so I just kind of went along with you guys.
And I think it was nice for the students too, to hear that — taking a phrase and yeah I’m going to keep going with this within the context of the song.
